goal: Step a template product release through build, candidate, plan, deploy, verify and accept, so no release is accepted without passing every protected job in order.

app.name: template-release-lifecycle
app.title: Release lifecycle
app.purpose: Give the next lifecycle state of a template product release from its current state, the pipeline event, whether the ref is protected and whether the attached evidence is complete.

fields.name: state
fields.means: the lifecycle state the release is in now

fields.name: event
fields.means: the prismpm.yml job that runs next

fields.name: ref
fields.means: whether the triggering branch or tag is protected

fields.name: evidence
fields.means: whether the deployment state and release evidence the job requires are attached

meanings.built: built once by the build job, without publication credentials
meanings.candidate: signed, promoted to candidate and pushed to the registry
meanings.planned: bound to observed target state by a deployment plan
meanings.deployed: deployed from the exact plan with deployment evidence attached
meanings.verified: post-deployment state and release evidence verified after a clean pull
meanings.accepted: conformance attached and promoted to accepted, the final state

rules.why: prismpm.yml: authorize-release requires branch or tag protection, then promote keyless-signs the development-to-candidate transition and pushes the candidate graph
prismpm.yml plan job: binds the immutable candidate release to observed target state without rebuilding
prismpm.yml deploy job: deploys the exact release and exact plan, then attaches deployment evidence
prismpm.yml verify-deployment: require observed deployment state and complete attached release evidence
prismpm.yml conformance then accept: every public feature case is attached before the candidate-to-accepted transition is signed
prismpm.yml: a job runs only when the jobs it needs succeeded, so any other event leaves a candidate release where it is
prismpm.yml: a job runs only when the jobs it needs succeeded, so any other event leaves a planned release where it is
prismpm.yml: a job runs only when the jobs it needs succeeded, so any other event leaves a deployed release where it is
prismpm.yml: a job runs only when the jobs it needs succeeded, so any other event leaves a verified release where it is
prismpm.yml: a job runs only when the jobs it needs succeeded, so any other event leaves a accepted release where it is

app.otherwiseWhy: prismpm.yml: without a protected ref the promote job never requests credentials, so a built release stays built

properties.why: authorize-release rejects publication from an unprotected ref
verify-deployment requires observed state and complete attached evidence
accept needs promote, deploy, verify-deployment and conformance first

stakeholders.name: Template adopter
stakeholders.text: Creates a repository from the template and needs prismpm.yml to take a release from build to accepted with nothing skipped.

stakeholders.name: Release approver
stakeholders.text: Guards the protected release and deployment environments and needs no unprotected ref or missing evidence to reach accepted.

components.name: PrismPM product pipeline
components.text: The reusable prismpm.yml workflow whose jobs are the lifecycle events.

components.name: GHCR
components.text: The registry the candidate and accepted graphs are pushed to and pulled from.

components.name: Sigstore
components.text: Keyless signing of the development-to-candidate and candidate-to-accepted transitions.

components.name: Deployment target
components.text: The modeled target, kubernetes-production by default, whose observed state the plan binds.

threats.name: Publication from an unprotected ref
threats.text: A push to an unprotected branch obtains release credentials and promotes a candidate.

control.name: Protected ref before promotion
control.text: Only a protected ref moves a built release to candidate.

threats.name: Acceptance without evidence
threats.text: A deployed release is marked verified or accepted while its deployment state or conformance evidence is missing.

control.name: Evidence before verification and acceptance
control.text: Missing evidence keeps the release where it is.

threats.name: Rebuilt release between steps
threats.text: A step rebuilds the product so the accepted digest differs from the built one.
threats.accepted: The app decides lifecycle states, not digests; prismpm.yml passes one immutable-reference from promote to every later job and never rebuilds.

quality.text: Each of the five prismpm.yml jobs after build (promote, plan, deploy, verify-deployment with conformance, accept) is one transition of the machine.
quality.measureText: Transitions on the shortest run from built to accepted.

quality.text: No single step takes a release past a job it needs.
quality.measureText: Transitions that move a release more than one lifecycle state forward.
